ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information, Act No. 10624, as amended; Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information, Presidential Decree No. 33167, as amended; Act on Regulation and Punishment of Concealment of Criminal Proceeds, Act No. 10623, as amended; Financial Services Commission Regulation on Beneficial Owner Identification and Customer Due Diligence; FATF Recommendations 10, 24 and 25, as implemented by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Commercial Register Extract) of the ultimate foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the issuing country is an Apostille Convention member: local notarization if required, followed by issuance of an Apostille certificate by the designated competent authority, then certified Korean translation. If the issuing country is not an Apostille member: local notarization, then consular legalization by the Republic of Korea embassy or consulate with territorial jurisdiction, then certified Korean translation. Never chain Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the ultimate foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or competent business registrar in the country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille-only path for Hague Apostille Convention states; Consular Legalization-only path for non-member states. The selected path depends solely on the issuing country's membership and must not combine both methods. A certified Korean translation is mandatory.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and/or Power of Attorney authorizing formation of the Korean Yuhan Hoesa and appointment of its local representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the ultimate foreign shareholder or its duly authorized corporate officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If executed in an Apostille state: notarize the signatures, affix an Apostille from the state secretary of state or other competent authority, then translate into Korean. If executed in a non-Apostille state: notarize and submit to the Korean embassy/consulate for consular legalization, then translate. The two authentication paths are mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum and Articles of the ultimate foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ultimate foreign shareholder; certified by its corporate secretary or registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Same parallel path: Apostille for member jurisdictions, Consular Legalization for non-members, with certified Korean translation after authentication. Apostille and consular legalization must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the ultimate shareholder and each beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Regulated commercial bank holding the UBO's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank-issued letter must be notarized if required by the bank's jurisdiction; if the state is an Apostille member, affix an Apostille; otherwise consular legalization by the Korean mission. The authenticated letter must be translated into Korean and dated within 90 days before filing.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before onboarding any shareholder, director, or beneficial owner, the Korean LLC's formation counsel must screen against the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit watchlist, the UN Security Council consolidated list, US OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, the EU consolidated list, UK OFSI consolidated list, and the Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act designations. Politically exposed persons, foreign PEPs, immediate family and close associates must undergo enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, senior management approval, and continuous transaction monitoring for at least 36 months. Negative media, adverse regulatory history, sanctions exposure, and shell-company risk indicators must be documented in the customer due diligence file before capital contribution.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea (i-registry.go.kr) and the Commercial Registration Information System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Korean Commercial Act and Commercial Registration Rules, the registered name of a Yuhan Hoesa must be written in the local Korean script (Hangul). A foreign name may be used in parallel but the register entry requires a phonetic Hangul transliteration. The statutory four-tier naming sequence is: (1) distinctive proprietary element; (2) business activity descriptor, which is customary for wholesale eyewear distribution; (3) legal form suffix Yuhan Hoesa; and (4) a locational or serial disambiguator when the identical name is pre-registered in the same registry district. Roman alphabet and numerals may appear only within the distinctive element after transliteration permission, and never as the legal-form suffix.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the commercial registry rejects the proposed name, the applicant must first obtain the written reason from the registration officer. A corrective re-filing with a different distinctive element is the fastest remedy. If the applicant contests the rejection, its Korean attorney must file an appeal with the district court having territorial jurisdiction over the registry within two weeks of the notice, under the Commercial Registration Act. For rejections characterized as administrative refusals, preserve all rights by filing an administrative litigation petition within 90 days under the Administrative Litigation Act. The appeal must attach the rejection notice, corrected articles, proof of name search, and a legal memorandum demonstrating the absence of identity with or deception against pre-registered trade names. No appeal fee is returned, and the proposed name remains unprotected until a new register entry is completed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox alone is not a compliant registered office for an operating wholesale distributor of ophthalmic eyewear frames under ISIC 4646. Korean commercial registration requires a domestic principal office. In practice, the National Tax Service and regulated banks reject a pure virtual office for VAT registration, corporate account opening, and tax invoice issuance. Banks applying the Real-Name Financial Transaction Act and financial information reporting rules treat a serviced address as valid only if accompanied by a physical lease, signboard, personnel, and the ability to receive original documents. For this industry, virtual office use is permissible only as an auxiliary postal address, never as the sole statutory registered office or commercial substance location.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for expected presence: physical lease in the company's name; company signboard at the door; designated employee or corporate officer available during business hours; local telephone and company email; utility bills or common area maintenance bills; actual business documents, stock or distribution support records; and evidence of conformity to the registered business purpose. Quantified risk: a standalone virtual office without these indicia carries a 35-50% probability of an unannounced National Tax Service or district tax office inspection within the first operating year; a fully equipped serviced office with signboard and staff reduces that risk to approximately 10-15%. Municipal registry officers also conduct postal verification and occasional field visits to confirm the head office before approving post-incorporation registrations.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Local Tax Act and Local Education Tax Act statutory tariff (0.4% registration tax plus 0.2% local education tax on paid-in capital)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of Korean articles of incorporation and parent company resolutions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notary Fees Act tariff and prevailing notarial market rate for bilingual documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority in each issuing state or the Republic of Korea embassy/consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official fee schedule per document; assumes five notarized instruments, exclusive of courier fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Court-certified Korean translation of UBO and corporate due diligence documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Foreign investment report, name clearance, and bank pre-account opening legal support
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean law firm engaged by the formation agent

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Part V 'Limited Liability Company', Articles 543 through 587, particularly Article 543 (Formation), Article 544 (Articles of Incorporation), Article 552 (Registration of Incorporation), and Article 560 (Capital), together with the Corporate Registration Regulations and the Electronic Government Act for online registry filings.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Office of the District Court, a branch of the Court Administration Office under the Supreme Court of Korea; online filings are handled through the i-Register national corporate registry portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation Registration with the Articles of Incorporation and paid-in capital verification certificate attached as statutory annexes.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Korean law does not impose a statutory minimum paid-in capital for a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company). Each founding member must subscribe for and fully pay the value of capital contributions before incorporation registration. The paid-in capital amount must be deposited into a dedicated bank deposit account in the company's proposed name, maintained as a blocked deposit until registration is completed, and verified by a balance certificate. No government escrow account is required; any commercial bank chartered under the Korean Banking Act may hold the deposit.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF YUHAN HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY)

PREAMBLE: At a meeting duly convened and held on the ____ day of ______, 20____, at the registered office of Yuhan Hoesa (the 'Company'), under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea and the Company's Articles of Incorporation, all founding members and statutory officers were present or validly represented, a quorum existed throughout, and the following resolutions were adopted unanimously.

RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the Company under the name 'Yuhan Hoesa' be, and it hereby is, ratified and confirmed; that the Articles of Incorporation, executed by all founding members, be approved and adopted in final form; and that the total subscribed capital of ______ Korean Won as stated in the Articles of Incorporation be accepted as the capital of the Company.

RESOLVED, that each member's capital contribution has been fully subscribed and paid in cash to the Company's designated capital deposit account at ______ Bank, and that the Deposit Certificate dated ______, issued by said bank, is conclusive evidence of the receipt and custody of the paid-in capital.

RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be situated at ______, ______ District, ______ City, Republic of Korea, subject to the exclusive registration jurisdiction of the ______ District Court Registration Office; and that the Company is authorized to establish branches, warehouses, and representative offices in any jurisdiction as business exigencies require.

RESOLVED, that the following persons are appointed as statutory officers with immediate effect: [Name], Executive Representative Director; [Name], Financial Director; and [Name], Supervisory Director, each to hold office until removed or replaced by a subsequent resolution duly adopted by the members.

RESOLVED, that the Executive Representative Director be, and is hereby, vested with full power and authority to execute and file all instruments, applications, declarations, and registrations before the District Court Registration Office, the National Tax Service, local municipal authorities, fire safety agencies, labor authorities, banks, customs brokers, and all other governmental and commercial institutions; to open, maintain, and operate domestic and foreign bank accounts and electronic settlement platforms; to negotiate, execute, and deliver leases, purchase agreements, distribution agreements, and financing instruments; and to employ professional advisers, notaries, customs agents, and registered public accountants as may be necessary to conduct the wholesale international distribution of ophthalmic eyewear frames.

RESOLVED, that all preliminary acts previously performed by the founding members and organizers in connection with corporate name search, preparation of documents, capital deposit, and pre-formation contracts be, and they hereby are, ratified, adopted, and confirmed as acts of the Company.

RESOLVED, that the Company's legal counsel be directed to prepare authenticated excerpts of this resolution and to record the same with the corporate registry, the corporate bank, and any government authority before which evidence of authority is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search, Reservation, and Drafting of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Online Registration Office (i-Register) and appointed South Korean attorney or certified legal draftsman
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform an exact-match Korean corporate name search on the i-Register portal and, if available, request reservation of the proposed corporate name in the name of Yuhan Hoesa. Engage a South Korean attorney or certified legal draftsman to prepare the Articles of Incorporation, which must contain the trade name, corporate purpose restricted to wholesale international distribution of ophthalmic eyewear frames, the address of the registered office, total subscribed capital, each member's contribution, method of representation, number and appointment of directors, supervisory director, and rules concerning transfer of capital contributions and amendment of articles. All founding members must execute the articles and affix personal seals, and each member must sign a capital subscription form and incorporation consent letter.
required_dossiers: Proposed Articles of Incorporation in final draft
Corporate name search certificate or name reservation receipt
Founding members' valid passports or national identity cards
Capital subscription forms executed by each member
Incorporation consent letter signed by all members
Power of attorney if an agent is appointed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search is rejected for identical or confusingly similar names, alter the proposed corporate name and re-file the search. If the registry or attorney identifies deficiencies in the articles, the attorney will amend and re-issue the draft; no additional notarization is required for a limited liability company unless the members resolve to restrict capital contribution transfers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening Capital Deposit Account and Full Payment of Subscribed Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank chartered under the Banking Act of the Republic of Korea (e.g., Kookmin Bank, Shinhan Bank, Woori Bank, Hana Bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary deposit account in the proposed corporate name at a commercial bank located in the Republic of Korea. Deliver the Articles of Incorporation, capital subscription form, and incorporation consent letter to the bank for identity verification. Instruct each founding member to remit fully the entire amount of subscribed capital into the designated blocked deposit account without using loans or third-party funds unless the articles permit. Obtain a Korean bank Certificate of Deposit or balance certificate issued in the name of the entity, showing account number, deposit date, and immutable holding until registration completion. Retain this certificate for submission to the District Court Registration Office.
required_dossiers: Valid identification of all founding members
Draft Articles of Incorporation presenting the capital structure
Capital subscription form endorsed by each member
Corporate name reservation receipt or name search certificate
Bank deposit application form and source-of-funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires supplementary anti-money-laundering information, provide the requested ownership and source-of-funds evidence and amend the deposit instruction. If the deposit certificate displays an incorrect corporate name, return the certificate to the bank for reissuance. If the funds are not fully credited, members must remit the shortfall and the freeze period restarts from the date of complete funding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing Incorporation Registration with the District Court Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Court Registration Office having jurisdiction over the registered office address, filed through the i-Register online portal or the court registry window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation registration application to the competent District Court Registration Office either physically or electronically through i-Register. Attach the notarized or sealed Articles of Incorporation, capital deposit certificate, list of members, capital contribution ledger, written appointment and written acceptance of each statutory officer, and evidence of payment of court registration tax and local education surtax. The registration officer will review all documents for conformity with the Commercial Act; after approval, the court enters the company into the corporate register and issues the certificate of completed incorporation registration. Obtain certified copies of the register and corporate seal certificate.
required_dossiers: Execution copy of the Articles of Incorporation
Bank Certificate of Deposit for paid-in capital
Capital contribution ledger and member list
Written appointment and acceptance of directors and supervisory director
Registration tax remittance receipt
Application for corporate registration and power of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or suspended, comply with the court's written correction order by filing supplementary documents within the prescribed cure period. If rejection is final after correction, file a new application with proper documentation. An immediate appeal lies against the registration rejection in accordance with the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act within the statutory appeal window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the National Tax Service and Tax-Related Post-Incorporation Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the registered office address, filed through the Hometax online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 20 business days after incorporation registration, file a Business Registration application with the competent District Tax Office using the Hometax portal. Attach the certificate of completed incorporation registration, certified copy of registered articles, corporate seal certificate, identification of the Executive Representative Director, and lease contract for the registered office. The tax office will issue the Business Registration Certificate and assign a unique corporate tax identification number, VAT registration status, and business classification code under ISIC 4646. Apply simultaneously for electronic tax invoice issuance through Hometax, employment and industrial accident insurance registration, and pension scheme registration.
required_dossiers: Certificate of completed incorporation registration
Certified copy of registered Articles of Incorporation
Corporate seal certificate
Executive Representative Director's identity document
Lease agreement for registered office
Business registration application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office requires additional dossiers, upload them through Hometax and respond to any clarification request. If the application is rejected based on incorrect business classification, submit a corrective application with the correct ISIC and NAICS codes. Administrative appeals may be filed with the National Tax Service Board of Tax Appeals if the rejection is maintained.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Bank Account Activation and Operational Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank; Korea Customs Service for importer/exporter registration if cross-border trade is intended; local fire station under the National Fire Agency; Ministry of Employment and Labor for occupational safety
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Activate the corporate operating bank account after presenting the Certificate of Incorporation, Business Registration Certificate, corporate seal certificate, and the First Board Resolution appointing signatories. If the company will import or export ophthalmic eyewear frames, register the company as an importer/exporter with the Korea Customs Service and obtain a customs clearance code. For any leased storage or distribution showroom, submit the floor plan and lease documents to the local fire station and apply for the appropriate fire safety certificate; also register the workplace with the Ministry of Employment and Labor and complete a workplace hazard assessment.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Business Registration Certificate
Corporate seal certificate and bank account opening forms
First Board Resolution appointing bank signatories
Korea Customs Service application and representative identity documents for importer/exporter registration
Lease contract and floor plan for any warehouse or showroom
Workplace hazard assessment form for labor approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account application due to incomplete resolution excerpt, obtain a certified board resolution excerpt from the attorney. If Korea Customs Service queries the application, correct the requested HS classification and re-submit. If the local fire station issues a deficiency notice, cure the listed fire-safety defects and schedule a re-inspection; if labor authorities require corrective measures, implement them and file the revised hazard assessment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Local District (Gu) Office Business Registration Section, National Tax Service, National Fire Agency, Ministry of Employment and Labor, and Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea; no sector-specific industrial permit is required because the activity is wholesale distribution.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Registration Certificate issued under Article 8 of the Value-Added Tax Act, accompanied by any applicable importer/exporter registration from Korea Customs Service; no separate manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or dedicated distribution license applies to the wholesale international distribution of ophthalmic eyewear frames.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea, Environmental Impact Assessment Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Wholesale distribution is not listed as an EIA-requiring project type under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act; no full EIA or environmental registration is required for pure wholesale trading. If the company later develops or operates a dedicated warehouse exceeding the regional threshold, a primary environmental review or small-scale environmental assessment may be triggered under the Act on Assessment of Environmental Impacts.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, stack emissions, or hazardous waste are generated by wholesale distribution of acetate eyeglass frames. If a private warehouse is established, sanitary wastewater must comply with applicable municipal sewer discharge standards under the Water Environment Conservation Act; general effluent thresholds are BOD/COD 40 mg/L, suspended solids 40 mg/L, total nitrogen 40 mg/L, and total phosphorus 4 mg/L. Incidental volatile organic compound emissions from cleaning or solvent use, if any, must meet the Clean Air Conservation Act's permissible emission standards for small-scale facilities, and any waste solvent must be transported by a licensed hazardous-waste carrier under the Wastes Control Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate under the Fire-Fighting System Installation and Maintenance Act, obtained from the local fire station for the premises. If the leased premises contain a warehouse or showroom with total floor area above the local threshold, a civil-defense shelter designation and approved evacuation plan are required. Workplace clearance requires registration of each workplace with the Ministry of Employment and Labor, completion of a workplace hazard assessment, installation of fire extinguishers and emergency lighting, mandatory occupational accident insurance subscription, and appointment of a workplace safety supervisor if the workplace has five or more employees, all in accordance with the Occupational Safety and Health Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of South Korea (NTS) via the Home Tax Service (HTS) electronic portal at www.hometax.go.kr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity or a Korean entity with foreign ownership must apply for a Korean business registration certificate (Sa-eop-ja-deung-luk-jeung) at the local NTS district office having jurisdiction over the domestic place of business or the authorized domestic agent. For a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), the representative or a duly authorized tax agent must file the registration application under Article 168 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, supplying the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, foreign investment report or notarized ownership evidence, a domestic registered address or place of an effective fixed place of business, proof of the domestic agent's appointment (where applicable), and a copy of the passport or foreign corporate registration certificate. The NTS then issues a 10-digit business registration number, which functions as both the TIN and VAT registration number. Effective from an operational standpoint, VAT registration is automatic upon business registration for a VAT-entrepreneur; however, a non-resident without any domestic place of business but required to collect Korean VAT on cross-border supplies of services shall separately register as a foreign entrepreneur within six months of the date of supply via the HTS portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None – Korean tax law does not allow a Yuhan Hoesa to make a check-the-box partnership pass-through election for its entire Korean tax profile. Hybrid mismatch and similar elections recognized under the OECD BEPS Action 2 recommendations are not generally available for standalone VAT purposes. The only relevant statutory election within the VAT framework is the ordinary taxpayer (general method) versus simplified taxpayer election; however, given the corporation's wholesale scale and cross-border distribution of ophthalmic frames, the simplified taxpayer regime is unavailable because the entity's revenue exceeds the statutory threshold, and no alternative entity-level classification election exists under the VAT Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general exemption threshold for VAT registration. Any entrepreneur, including a foreign entity making taxable supplies in Korea through a fixed place of business or a domestic agent, must register with the NTS from the date of business commencement. A simplified taxpayer threshold exists for individually owned small businesses receiving annual taxable turnover below KRW 80 million (KRW 48 million for most service industries, revised thresholds apply depending on the business sector); however, this does not apply to a Yuhan Hoesa carrying on international wholesale of optical frames. Foreign non-resident businesses without a domestic place of business are required to register only when making supplies subject to Korean VAT, particularly electronically supplied services or imported services that reverse-charge, but no statutory minimum turnover exemption is available for such registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT taxpayers must issue tax invoices (Seong-gum-gye-san-seo) electronically through the National Tax Service's electronic tax invoice system (Jeonja Seonggumgyesanseo) hosted on Home Tax Service. Issuance of an electronic tax invoice is mandatory for any transaction exceeding KRW 1,000,000 (including VAT) in the case of an electronic tax invoice obligation and for all registered corporations regardless of amount. The E-Tax Invoice must be transmitted to the NTS through the recommended API using the NTS-certified business accounting software or an open API using the certificate-based integrated authentication (Hanbo Geumseung Injeung). There is no independent fiscal clearance stamp or government real-time digital stamping server; instead, real-time anti-fraud validation is achieved through NTS e-tax invoice XML schema validations, electronic tax invoice issuance deadlines, and mandatory periodic VAT returns filed semi-annually. For exports, additional electronic customs clearance occurs via UNI-PASS of the Korea Customs Service (KCS), electronically linked to the NTS VAT export documentation system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated export of goods applies under Article 0 of the VAT Act when goods are sold to a foreigner or a foreign enterprise and are delivered from Korea to an overseas destination, whether through direct export, consignment sale through overseas bonded warehouses, or licensed local foreign trade transactions. For wholesale distribution of ophthalmic eyeglass frames, the seller must keep evidence that ownership of the goods has passed to a foreign buyer, that the goods have physically departed Korea, and that the sales proceeds are received in foreign currency. Digital services and intangible supplies are zero-rated only when actually supplied to a non-resident user outside Korea and supplied domestically only in an ancillary manner. A Yuhan Hoesa must also ensure the Korean customs officer approves the export declaration and the entity reports the export within the statutory VAT return periods.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export declaration receipt and Customs Export Declaration (Export Bill of Entry / Permitted Export Customs-Clearance Completion Certificate) issued via UNI-PASS by Korea Customs Service
Commercial invoice and detailed packing list
Bill of Lading (ocean) or Air Waybill (air) evidencing shipment to the foreign buyer
Contract or purchase order from the foreign buyer
Foreign Exchange Bank certificate evidencing repatriation of export proceeds, e.g. Inward Remittance Certificate or Export Foreign Exchange Sales Confirmation
Certificate of Origin only where required by trade agreement, not generally required for VAT zero-rating
Overseas bonded warehouse or customs transit records if applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service may jointly audit export zero-rating claims. Under the VAT Act and Framework Act on National Taxes, any export zero-rating improperly claimed results in immediate assessment of unpaid VAT with a 10% additional tax for non-payment or understatement; up to 20% additional tax for negligent underreporting; and up to 40% additional tax for fraudulent non-reporting or false claims. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the statutory foreign exchange collection period does not automatically revoke zero-rating if the exporter proves receipt through a deferred settlement authorized by a foreign exchange bank, but failure to keep the mandatory documentation or submission of false export declarations may trigger criminal sanctions under Article 276 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, including fines up to KRW 100 million and imprisonment up to three years, plus retrospective clawback of VAT refunded for up to five years from the original return filing date.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) acting through the Foreign Exchange Information System operated by the Korea Customs Service for trade-related foreign exchange transactions
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates an open capital account under the framework of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA) and its Enforcement Decree. The Korean won (KRW) is fully convertible for current account transactions, including trade in goods and services, dividends, and royalties, provided that supporting documents are filed with the designated foreign exchange bank. Capital account transactions are largely liberalized but remain subject to a prior declaration or reporting regime, particularly for inward direct investment, external borrowing, and acquisition of domestic securities by non-residents. There is no mandatory surrender requirement for export proceeds; Korea eliminated forced conversion in the 1990s, allowing exporters to hold foreign currency in designated foreign currency accounts (USD, EUR, JPY, etc.) domestically or abroad. Profit remittance is permitted through the 'trade settlement' or 'non-trade settlement' route, but the remitting bank will require an audited financial statement, tax clearance certificate from the National Tax Service (NTS), and a board resolution declaring dividends. Foreign exchange banks must report suspicious transactions to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) under the Financial Information Act. In practice, the convertibility is highly accessible for legitimate commercial entities, but banks conduct strict beneficial ownership identification, end-use verification, and source-of-funds checks for both inbound equity investments and outbound trade payments. For an optical eyewear wholesale entity, there are no industry-specific FX restrictions, but invoice authenticity and customs declaration matching (via the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system) are key validation points for bank compliance. The strategic risk is not non-convertibility but rather administrative friction from documentary mismatch and reporting thresholds, which can delay settlement unless treasury operations maintain meticulous trade documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, exporters must receive payment for exported goods within 6 months from the date of the export declaration, subject to extension by up to 2 years for capital equipment or projects. The full amount of foreign currency received must be either deposited into a domestic foreign currency account (to be used freely) or reported to the designated bank through the foreign exchange settlement system. Exporters are free to convert to KRW at any time or hold the proceeds in foreign currency; however, all receipts must be recorded with the underlying export declaration number (D/O No.) to satisfy the Korea Customs Service and the Bank of Korea's reporting requirements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Corporate Operating Settlement Account (KRW Current Account) with sub-limit Foreign Currency Account
Funded Foreign Direct Investment Capital Escrow Account (Foreign Currency) connected to KRW Corporate Account
Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW Demand Deposit) with Trade Services linkage
Foreign Investment Corporate Account (KRW/USD) for export collection and disbursement

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility and legally constrained. South Korea does not recognize third-country electronic money institutions (EMIs) or digital bank licenses issued in the EU/UK as valid payment service providers for domestic corporate accounts. Global EMIs such as Revolut Business, Wise, or Airwallex cannot open a local KRW account or provide a domestic account number for Yuhan Hoesa. Foreign EMIs may only operate as money transfer businesses under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act if they register with the Financial Services Commission (FSC), which effectively requires a local subsidiary and full licensing, a process unrealistic for a low-risk wholesaler. Domestic internet-only banks (KakaoBank, Toss Bank) are restricted to consumer and small business banking; they do not robustly support cross-border letters of credit, documentary collections, or foreign investment capital verification. The correct treasury rail remains a tier-1 traditional commercial bank with a dedicated corporate foreign exchange desk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Korean legal entity created by non-resident shareholders, at least one statutory director (or the foreign investor with signatory authority) must appear physically in-branch at the designated bank for initial account opening, due to the Real-Name Financial Transactions Act and the regulation requiring in-person verification of the representative. Remote consular proxy opening is not permitted for corporate accounts. The authorized signatory may alternatively be a resident director appointed under a power of attorney, but the power of attorney itself must be notarized and apostilled. The bank's compliance officer may conduct a video interview, but this supplements, not replaces, the mandatory physical appearance of the account signatory. Foreign investors are also required to obtain a Foreign Investment Certificate from an authorized bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, which itself requires the investor to submit board resolutions and incorporation documents before account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity when the ultimate shareholder is a natural person residing outside Korea and the entity is newly formed with no operating history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a certified group structure chart, individual passports of all shareholders above 25%, tax identification numbers from the home jurisdiction, audited financial statements of the parent (if any), and a written declaration of source of funds for the inbound equity injection, including bank statements showing the funds origin and a notarized board resolution of the Korean entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between the declared business purpose (wholesale distribution of ophthalmic eyewear frames) and the actual payment routing to multiple unknown foreign beneficiaries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide executed purchase orders with real counterparties, proforma invoices from manufacturers, logistics contracts and bill of lading samples, plus an annual business plan describing the supply chain. The bank will also require registration of the business with the Korea Customs Service and a copy of the audited financial statements after the first fiscal year to substantiate the transaction flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential trade-based money laundering red flag if export invoice prices deviate significantly from industry benchmarks for acetate eyeglass frames
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a transfer pricing policy in line with OECD guidelines, retain independent valuation reports for the frames, and provide full manufacturer invoices, general price lists, and shipping insurance certificates. The entity must also execute a correlation between the customs declared value and the foreign exchange settlement amount, with reconciliation reports submitted to the bank quarterly.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Position of the entity as a shell/letterbox if the registered address is a virtual office and no operational substance is demonstrable
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement for a physical office or warehouse, employment contracts for at least two local staff (e.g., operations manager and accountant), utility bills, and documentary evidence of participation in industry events. Banks accept a leased shared office if business records and a local representative are clearly identified.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital from a foreign shareholder must be wired via SWIFT MT103 to the designated foreign currency account of the Korean entity at a domestic bank. The remittance must carry a proper purpose code under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act—typically 'A4-1 (Investment)' or 'A4-2 (Acquisition of shares)'—and must be accompanied by a Korean Foreign Exchange Bank Certificate of Foreign Currency Purchase. The entity must first obtain a Foreign Investment Certificate from the receiving bank by submitting the investor's share acquisition application, power of attorney, and certificate of incorporation. Within 30 days after the receipt of funds, the entity must register the foreign investment with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy or its delegated authority. Capital verification is done through the bank's issuance of a 'Certificate of Paid-in Capital' after confirming the converted KRW deposited into the corporate account; this certificate serves as evidence for future dividend repatriation and for the commercial registry update.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For payment to overseas frame suppliers, the primary rail is SWIFT MT103 for open account settlements under a purchase invoice, using purpose code 'A2-2 (Import settlement)'. The bank requires the import declaration receipt (D/O) from the Korea Customs Service, an import license for medical devices if applicable, and the original commercial invoice. For high-value or first-time transactions, the entity may open an irrevocable Letter of Credit (Documentary Credit) via the bank's trade finance desk, cleared through SWIFT MT700; settlements under LC are executed via MT202/MT103 after presentation of compliant shipping documents. Documentary collections (DP/DA) are also permitted but require the remitting bank to process export bills through the national electronic platform. All outbound wires must be pre-notified to the bank's compliance division if the transaction exceeds USD 10,000 equivalent, with supporting documents retained for five years for audit.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla forward exchange contracts (USD/KRW) with a domestic commercial bank, limited to maturities of 12 months and based on real underlying trade exposure (i.e., the wholesale purchase/sale of acetate eyewear frames).

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permitted only through the onshore interbank market for non-trade capital flows; for trade-based hedging, the Korea Financial Supervisory Service encourages deliverable forwards instead. A corporate entity may execute NDFs with a recognized bank if it qualifies for such transactions under the FETA, but they are not the default instrument for a low-risk wholesaler.

Cross-currency swaps are permissible strictly for hedging long-term foreign currency liabilities (e.g., an overseas facility) but are restricted for speculative purposes; a treasury operation would need to document the underlying exposure and obtain the bank's FX derivative eligibility approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (including local income tax surcharge) submitted to the National Tax Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) / Regional Tax Office with jurisdiction over the registered head office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 for a calendar year-end fiscal year; within three months after the end of the fiscal year for a non-calendar year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% of the unpaid corporate tax; daily late-payment interest of 0.022% on the shortfall; additional 20% penalty for unreported income; administrative seizure of assets and criminal referral for tax evasion for repeated delinquency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements filing with the court registry (Commercial Act Article 447-4)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the Local District Court
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the annual general meeting of members, which must be held no later than three months after the fiscal year end; in a calendar-year company this is typically April 30 (if the members' meeting is held by March 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance penalty (administrative fine) up to KRW 5,000,000 under Commercial Act Article 635; a court order for compulsory filing may be issued; no automatic strike-off is available for this specific filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External auditor's report, where the mandatory audit threshold is met (filed with NTS and, when applicable, FSS/DART)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (DART) and National Tax Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted together with the corporate tax return by March 31 for calendar-year filers; the audit report must be issued by the date of the annual members' meeting, and DART submission must occur within 14 days after issuance for audit-target companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to KRW 50,000,000 for violation of the Act on External Audit of Companies; the NTS may reject the tax return as incomplete; penalty for missing DART filing ranges up to KRW 20,000,000 for non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Article 2 of the Act on External Audit of Companies, mandatory independent CPA audit is required if, at the end of the preceding fiscal year: (i) the total assets of the Yuhan Hoesa are KRW 5.0 billion or more; or (ii) the entity is designated as an audit target by the Securities and Futures Commission due to its total revenue, number of employees, financial structure, or public interest. For Korean wholesale companies, the asset threshold is the primary trigger; however, a company with total assets below the threshold may still be designated where its annual gross revenue exceeds KRW 10.0 billion and its operational complexity warrants audit protection.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for listed companies and for audit-target companies that are required to apply K-IFRS; unlisted small- and medium-sized wholesale entities may elect to apply Korean GAAP (K-GAAP) in accordance with the Korean Accounting Standards Board. Financial statements must be presented in Korean won and audited in accordance with Korean Standards on Auditing (KSA).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not impose a public UBO annual filing for domestic limited liability companies outside the financial and crypto sectors. The Yuhan Hoesa must maintain a current Register of Members and record any transfer of membership within 30 days of the transfer date (Commercial Act); the court registration office must then be updated via an application for registration of the transfer. If the company is registered as a foreign-invested enterprise, the foreign investor must file a change report with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (through an authorized bank within 30 days of any ownership change), and an annual foreign investment business report may also be required by the Ministry in the first quarter following the reporting year.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book / Resolution Book of Members and Directors

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - USD 1,200 per year for professional corporate secretarial and registered office services in Seoul (including court filing support).
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 10,000 per year for a small or medium-sized wholesale entity preparing K-GAAP financial statements, depending on transaction volume and complexity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top progressive rate (10% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 20% on KRW 200 million - KRW 20 billion; 22% on KRW 20 billion - KRW 300 billion; 24% over KRW 300 billion)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible Korea Free Economic Zones (FEZ) can provide 100% CIT exemption for the first 5 years and 50% for the following 2 years under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; Special Tax Treatment Control Act Article 10 allows 20-50% R&D deduction and tax credits; patent box-style high-tech technology income may benefit from reduced CIT rates; wholesale distributors of ophthalmic frames are ordinary taxable entities unless located in FEZ and satisfying FDI requirements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Primary form: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Return filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax system (www.hometax.go.kr); attachment includes financial statements, adjusting schedules and non-resident withholding schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (Corporate Tax Act Article 60); for a December 31 year-end, no later than March 31 of the following year; an automatic one-month extension is available upon application where the books are prepared or audited abroad.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Company identification and fiscal period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered corporate name, Korean business registration number, head office address, representative director and shareholder register, fiscal year start and end dates; classification of entity as a domestic corporation (Yuhan Hoesa LLC).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose every non-resident shareholder's legal name, residential address, domestic tax identification number, foreign tax identification number, percentage ownership and date of acquisition; attach proof of foreign currency remittance into Korea; where the LLC is 100% foreign-owned, file a beneficial ownership schedule to avoid nominee-shareholder abuse; use the exact English name from the Korean Commercial Register.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income statement rows: gross revenue from international wholesale distribution of acetate eyeglass frames and related optical accessories; purchase cost of frames from non-resident suppliers; import freight and duties; gross margin; selling, general and administrative expenses; operating profit; non-operating income and expenses; ordinary income before tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Record all intercompany sales on an arm's length basis; export sales to a foreign headquarters or related distributor remain fully taxable in Korea unless attributable to another permanent establishment; do not reduce revenue by arbitrary discounts or rebates to non-residents without contractual documentation; transfer-pricing adjustments to gross margin must be reflected in this reconciliation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of book net income to tax base: non-taxable income, non-deductible expenses, depreciation and impairment differences, entertainment expense disallowances, donation limitations, bad debt allowances, foreign exchange differences, and deemed losses/income from affiliated persons.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back excessive management fees, licence fees, service fees, interest, or rents paid, accrued, or imputed to non-resident related parties to the extent they exceed arm's length value or lack a valid invoice/contract; add back entertainment expenses above the statutory deduction threshold; expenses for the personal benefit of the foreign controlling shareholder are nondeductible and must be restored to income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Tax base and loss carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the corporate tax base: taxable income after all adjustments, less deductible retained losses from prior years, less tax-exempt income, plus special surcharges, resulting in the final net taxable base on which the tax rates are applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A domestic Korean LLC is taxed on worldwide income; do not apply a branch exemption; loss carryforward is constrained to the statutory 5-year limitation and cannot exceed the available proved net operating loss ledgers; if the loss was generated by a non-resident-owned conduit or shell activity lacking economic substance, the NTS is authorized to disallow the carryforward.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Tax calculation and tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of progressive corporate income tax rates; subtraction of tax credits including foreign tax credit, research and development credits, job creation credits, investment credits and electronic tax invoice credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign tax credit only for foreign taxes withheld in the sales-market jurisdiction on Korean-source income; attach a Foreign Tax Credit schedule, Foreign Tax Residency Certificate (TRC), receipt of payment and proof that the foreign tax was paid as an income tax; the credit is limited to Korean corporate tax attributable to foreign-source income; excess foreign taxes are not refundable but may be carried forward under national law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Local corporate tax and total tax payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the local corporate income tax surcharge, which is 10% of the national corporate income tax; total tax payable equals national tax plus local surtax, less interim taxes already paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean resident LLC is subject to the ordinary national and local corporate taxes; dividends or profit repatriations to non-resident shareholders are not deductible and must not reduce the Box 6 liability; any withheld non-resident dividend tax is outside this corporate income tax account and must be reported separately in the withholding schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Non-resident withholding and transfer-pricing schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Supplementary attachments: details of domestic-source income paid to non-residents (dividends, interest, royalties), transfer-pricing disclosures, local file/master file notification, and country-by-country reporting notification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report every dividend, interest or royalty payment made to non-resident shareholders/related persons; attach the DTA relief application and TRC before the withholding payment date; if treaty relief is not approved by the date of payment, withhold 22% statutory tax and file a withholding return; for intercompany goods transactions exceeding the KRW 10 billion threshold, attach the Local File/Master File schedules to prevent non-filing penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or unfaithful filing triggers penalties under the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 47-3 (20% of unpaid tax for non-filing), Article 47-2 (10% for an unfaithful return, 40% for a fraudulent or false return), and daily delinquency surcharges under the National Tax Collection Act until the claim is satisfied; criminal referral under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act can lead to imprisonment for up to five years and a fine of up to five times the tax evaded; non-resident withholding omissions carry an additional withholding negligence penalty of 10% plus personal liability for the responsible director.
